texts.facts: The brief facts of the case as per the plaintiff are that he is the resident of G-76-C, Shaheen Bagh, Kalindi Kunj Main Road, Shaheen Bagh, Jamia Nagar, New Delhi and is running a shop of readymade garments from the said address for his livelihood. It is averred by the plaintiff that defendant no. 1 and defendant no. 2 are situated on both sides of plaintiff's residence and since Mohd. It is further averred by the plaintiff that both the defendants have large number of cooking and supporting staff who continue to carry out the cooking activities throughout the night making lot of noise, spreading foul smell, fog and smoke all over the area which is disturbing and hazardous. It is further the case of the plaintiff that defendants are in the practice of illegal storage of large quantity of LPG cylinders for industrial use, large size drums, cooking pot, oil and other cooking chemicals in large quantity along- with chemicals, spices and non-vegetarian material without following the rules and regulations and other applicable municipal laws, norms and guidelines. . 2. Further, even though plaintiff has claimed that defendants are undertaking commercial activities in a residential area, he himself has admitted that he is running a commercial shop from his residence. Plaintiff has further failed to examine any witness from the same locality to support his version of the story. Furthermore, during his cross-examination, plaintiff has stated, "Restaurants are not operational throughout night. They close by 11:00PM. Again said by 1:00AM, however, food is cooked and prepared all night". This statement of the plaintiff is in clear contradiction of the averment of the plaintiff as through his plaint, plaintiff has claimed that defendants are running their business throughout the night for sale on the spot or supply to other branches. Plaintiff has relied upon Ex.PW1/8 to support his claim that defendants are cooking food at the location in question for their various branches, however, perusal of Ex.PW1/8 merely shows food being delivered or taken in/out and does not substantiate the claim that food is being delivered for other branches. Furthermore, Ex.PW1/8 is a picture of broad day light and thus, cannot in any matter support the claim of food being delivered at night. Accordingly, plaintiff has failed to substantiate the claim of nuisance. Additionally, plaintiff has not produced anything on record to prove personal injuries caused to him by the business activities run by the defendants and in such a case, defendants cannot be directed to shut down their business.
